framing: An answer is only as useful as its path back to the source
paragraphs: A support specialist needs one decision: can this stale service-account key be rotated automatically? The index holds an obsolete rule, a current rule with two conditions, and a browser-session policy with a tempting thirty-day limit. A fluent answer can pick the wrong number and sound entirely sure of itself.

Ingestion and chunking made those sources searchable. Serving a request adds a new job: keeping the link between the caller, the right revision of the source, the passage in the prompt, and the claim in the answer. Any stage can weaken that link while every network call succeeds.

We build a small policy service so you can see each decision. It follows a permitted child to its parent section, checks both conditions, and tells a supported no apart from having nothing to go on. Then we write the prompt itself, run it on a real model, and catch an invented citation in code.

This gives you something stable to improve. Better search in the chapters ahead will change which candidates arrive, and the service will still have to explain why each passage was allowed and how it supports the answer.
outcomes: Carry caller scope, source revisions, and complete rule conditions through a RAG request.
Tell apart candidate recall, faithfulness, a supported denial, and an abstention.
Use a request trace to find the first stage that failed, on accuracy or on latency.
question: What has to survive between a searchable policy passage and a recommendation someone can safely act on?
